scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A query, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is checked over the visit infos of the build that plans it (`table_privilege::check_plan_privilege`: a query's before it is optimized, a DML's once it is built, a point plan's through `check_fast_plan_privilege`). PREPARE and a new non-prepared plan-cache entry still collect their `VisitInfos` with the visit-only builds `query_visit_info` / `dml_visit_info` (`Session::collect_table_privileges`) and build their plans separately, where Go's `GeneratePlanCacheStmtWithAST` keeps those of its one `PlanBuilder.Build`; and an INSERT's visit infos come from the separate builders of its target, source and values, where Go's `buildInsert` has one `PlanBuilder`

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: 53 of Go's 86 `ddl.executor` methods (`pkg/ddl/executor.go`) have no counterpart, `DoDDLJob` / `DoDDLJobWrapper` among them: a statement is lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`, then a `lower_*` builder) and submitted by `submit_built_job` / `submit_persisted_job_with_retry`; the missing methods include `AlterSchema`, `CreateTableWithInfo` / `BatchCreateTableWithInfo`, `RebaseAutoID`, `ShardRowID`, `ChangeColumn`, `RenameColumn`, `RenameIndex`, `DropView`, `CreatePrimaryKey`, `LockTables`, `CleanupTableLock`, `RepairTable`, `CreateSequence` / `AlterSequence`, the placement-policy, check-constraint, masking-policy, TTL, cache and attribute alters

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`); with it the status port's `/ingest/*` routes (Go `IngestConcurrencyHandler` over `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters) are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: Cancellation follows Go's `convertJob2RollbackJob` for every action the worker runs. A columnar (vector, inverted, full-text) index is checked against its table as Go's `createColumnarIndex` does (`add_index.rs` `create_columnar_index`, `checkTableTypeForColumnarIndex`), but on a table with a columnar replica this node builds no `ActionAddColumnarIndex` job: `onCreateColumnarIndex` (TiFlash schema sync, `checkColumnarIndexProcess`) and its `rollingbackAddColumanrIndex` are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A multi-schema change has no `promoteProxyKVDiskFullPause`, whose only producer (`autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the DXF add-index task) Rust lacks (D02, O10)

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A persisted DDL job step takes its schema from the owner's `InfoCache` at the step's version (Go `jobCtx.infoCache`) with the job's involved schemas reloaded whole from meta (`overlay_job_schemas`: each `DBInfo` and every table in whatever state), and its action handlers look objects up in that catalog, where Go's handlers point-read the job's objects through `jobCtx.metaMut` (`checkSchemaExistAndCancelNotExistJob`, `GetTableInfoAndCancelFaultJob`)

Root HashAgg is Go's `HashAggExec` (`tidb-executor-aggregate/src/agg_hash_executor.rs`: fetcher, partial workers shuffling one mapper per final worker, final workers, `parallelHashAggSpillHelper` spill), and its serial and parallel memory are Go's to the byte for global and pushed-down aggregates (`sum(a)` 12.6 KB, `b, count(a) ... group by b` 13.5 KB, `count(distinct b)` 12.4 KB) except a grouped scan-fed one (`a, group_concat(b) ... group by a` 14.0 KB where a fresh Go session's holds 14.8 KB) and an index-fed `count(distinct a)` (12.3 KB / 12.6 KB), for a reason not yet found (Go's `groupKeyPool` / `partialResultsBufferPool` recycle buffers across statements, so a later statement in one Go session charges more); a cop-side aggregation with no pushed form (`pushed_partial_aggregation` refuses its function kind, or an argument the pushdown catalog cannot lower: X01) runs in this tier on Go's TiDB-tier `HashAggExec` / `StreamAggExec`, where Go always runs it in the coprocessor; in the suites and the corpus only a TiFlash fragment's aggregates (M01) reach it

`IndexLookUpExecutor`'s memory and RU v2 are Go's, on every run: the double read (`IndexRangeSourceExec`, `access_path.rs` `IndexLookUpMemory`) owns a tracker labelled with its plan that each open attaches to the statement's, charged with its index ranges' KV ranges (`buildTableKeyRanges`), the index worker's responses (`LabelForIndexWorker`) and each table task's `executeTask` bytes (`cap(handles)` and the handles, the task's `TableReaderExecutor` at 768 plus its KV ranges and `dagPB.Size()`, the chunks it fills, `task.rows`, a keep-order `indexOrder` and `rowIdx`), the next task releasing the last; each task's reader records `TableReaderExecutor` into the parent's accumulator. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and `tidb_mem_quota_query` match Go for integer, keep-order `_tidb_rowid` and clustered handles (`tests_explain.rs` `an_index_lookup_charges_its_tasks_like_go`). Remaining: an unordered lookup whose output lacks the handle appends it to the table request to associate rows (`SELECT c FROM t USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 1`, or `SELECT *` over a `_tidb_rowid` table), so its DAG and chunks are a column wider than Go's (2.54 KB where Go shows 2.14 KB); a task (one `next_lookup_batch` window) is cut at the batch size where Go's `extractTaskHandles` keeps the whole chunk `readFromChunk` hands it (`ReuseIntermChk`), so a small batch splits Go's one task (6 rows at `tidb_index_lookup_size` 2: Go one 2.58 KB task, this port three, 4.92 KB), and a window spans the partitions Go gives a task each (`p ... PARTITION BY HASH(a) PARTITIONS 2`, `b > 1`: Go two tasks, 5.13 KB, this port one, 4.29 KB); a task the store answers without a table reader (`LookupFetch::LocalFallback`: a dirty transaction's read, a refused remote shape) charges nothing; a `LocalIndexLookUp`'s index-side responses hold handles where Go's hold the completed rows; and the reader is one source shared with `IndexReader` and index-merge partials, its tasks windows of one `LookupPipeline` over a `LanePool`, not Go's index worker, table workers and `resultCh`

`IndexJoin` and `IndexHashJoin` are Go's `IndexLookUpJoin` and `IndexNestedLoopHashJoin` (`join/index_lookup_join.rs`, `join/index_lookup_hash_join.rs`: outer and inner workers over `Joiner`), with Go's task memory and matching; the fused `JoinExec` lookup strategy is gone. Two gaps remain: Go's `IndexLookUpMergeJoin` executor (and `PhysicalIndexMergeJoin`'s `KeyOff2KeyOffOrderByIdx`, `CompareFuncs`, `NeedOuterSort`, `Desc`) is unported -- neither planner builds one on this branch, and the builder refuses the kind; and Go's `IndexJoinExecutorBuilder` builds each task's inner executor afresh, where this port's inner workers re-seed one shared `IndexLookupSource` under a lock unless the lookup forks (a common-handle prefix)

The embedded store's coprocessor runs every DAG through Go's `mppExec` chain (`tidb-unistore-cophandler` `mpp.rs`, `mpp_exec.rs`), filters condition by condition as Go's `VectorizedFilter` does, and answers errors as `genRespWithMPPExec` does (`SelectResponse.error`, a conflict's `OtherError`, an unsupported executor's `OtherError`), but the index-lookup push-down is absent end to end: a `LocalIndexLookUp` plan (the `index_lookup_pushdown` hint, `tidb_index_lookup_pushdown_policy`) runs as this tier's own double read (`physical_builder.rs` `lower_index_lookup_selections`) where Go's `IndexLookUpExecutor` sends one `IndexLookUp` DAG and reads its rows and `IntermediateOutputs`, and this tier's coprocessor refuses `buildIndexLookUp`

A TiKV reader builds its DAG from its access path's scan request (`cop_reader.rs`; `cop_plan_ids_for` matches executors to the pushed nodes by kind) where Go's `constructDAGReq` lowers the reader's pushed plan one node per executor (`ToPB`). A pushed TopN (a reader's, or an IndexLookUp's index side) reaches the coprocessor through the scan's offer, its `ByItem`s expressions over the scan's output as `PhysicalTopN.ToPB` lowers them

A projection's vectorized result column takes the shape its Go builtin's `vecEval*` gives it (`chunk_executor.rs`: `Resize*`, `Reserve*` and appends, one argument evaluated into it, a column's `CopyReconstruct`) for arithmetic, comparisons and `IN`, logic, `NOT`/`IS NULL`/`IS TRUE`, casts, `IF`/`IFNULL`/`CASE`/`COALESCE`, numeric and temporal `GREATEST`/`LEAST`, the math, time, JSON, info and common string builtins, `ADDTIME`/`SUBTIME`, `CONVERT_TZ`, `ANY_VALUE` and `SETVAR`; a tree holding a builtin outside that table still appends row by row: `GREATEST`/`LEAST` over strings (Go's `GreatestString` ping-pongs two buffers and copy-constructs `result` from the last one, so `SELECT greatest(c, 'x'), a+1` over 100 rows peaks at 12.1 KB where Go's is 12.4 KB) and the less common string, encryption and miscellaneous builtins. The values still come from the row and batch evaluators rather than Go's `vecEval*` kernels, and `IF`'s row fallback when its condition warns (`fallbackEval*`, which resizes) is not modelled

The session's reusable chunk allocator is Go's (`Session::chunk_alloc`, Go `clientConn.chunkAlloc`: installed per statement as `NewSyncAllocator(alloc)` under `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk`, never for an internal `InRestrictedSQL` statement, reset between statements and recreated after a failed one, each statement's validity its own), executors take it as `ExecutorMeta::alloc_pool` (Go `AllocPool`) for `NewChunk` / `TryNewCacheChunk` / `NewChunkWithCapacity`, and Go's `NewFirstChunk` sites (`Executor::new_first_chunk`: projection workers, hash-join probe and result chunks, index-hash-join results, shuffle holders, the drained record set) allocate outside it, so memory charges match Go's in sequence (`a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`, `explain_analyze_dml_roots_report_their_executor_stats_and_memory_like_go`). Remaining: executors built outside the physical builder's `meta` (`ExecutorMeta::new` in other crates) allocate fresh; parallel apply's chunks, whose executor shape differs from Go's, are unmapped; the reuse hook's `StmtCtx.SetUseChunkAlloc` (`@@last_sql_use_alloc`) is not driven by allocation
IMPORT INTO refuses (`tidb-session/src/dispatch.rs`)

Binary plans carry Go's runtime statistics (`binaryOpFromFlatOp`). The statement summary's and slow log's plan and binary plan are rendered after the statement ran (`getEncodedPlan`, `getBinaryPlan`). The brief binary plan is re-encoded when the process goes to sleep (`SetProcessInfo` at `ComSleep`, for routed statements too). `EXPLAIN FOR CONNECTION` decodes the brief plan of a target with no `RuntimeStatsColl` or with an `Execute` plan (a text `EXECUTE`, `shouldDecodeBriefBinaryPlan`). All of this matches a Go tidb-server over the wire (`unistore_cop.rs` `the_summary_plans_carry_the_statements_runtime_stats_like_go`, `explain_for_connection_renders_the_targets_runtime_stats_like_go`). Remaining: the operators of a cached prepared write charge different memory under `EXECUTE`. The root of `update t set b=? where id=?` shows 387 Bytes where Go shows 638 Bytes. The `TableReader` of a cached `update t set b=b+1 where b > ?` shows 272 Bytes where Go shows 270 Bytes. The same statements unprepared show 1.11 KB and 272 Bytes on both servers.

A text `EXECUTE` of a cached prepared write runs inside the `EXECUTE`'s one statement lifecycle (`execute_cached_prepared_dml` no longer opens a nested `run_with_columns_using`), so it has one `StatementMemory` tracker, as Go's one `StmtCtx` does. Remaining: a binary-protocol `EXECUTE` (`cluster_session_node` `execute`) binds its cached point, SELECT or DML plan before the statement lifecycle begins, so a plan-cache miss builds its planner context under the previous statement's authority, which `begin_statement_execution` then retires. Go's `ExecuteStmt` runs `PrepareTxnCtx` and `ResetContextOfStmt` before `Compile`'s plan-cache lookup.

Request units are never accounted for a statement's requests. Over the wire, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` reports `RU:0.00` for every statement, reads and writes alike, where Go reports what its resource-group controller's `KVCalculator` charged: `RU:0.47` for a point read, `RU:3.94` for a point UPDATE, `RU:3.54` for an INSERT. The controller is started and installed as the resource-control interceptor (`init_resource_groups_controller`), so the gap lies in how a statement's requests carry its `RUDetails` to the interceptor (client-go `util.RUDetailsCtxKey`). A write's root now carries Go's `RuntimeStatsWithCommit` (`FinishExecuteStmt`, before the connection goes to sleep: `unistore_cop.rs` `a_write_root_carries_its_commit_stats_like_go`).
findings.go_owner: `pkg/executor/explain.go` (`RUDetails` in the runtime stats), client-go `internal/client` resource-control interceptor and `util.RUDetailsCtxKey`, PD `client/resource_group/controller` (`KVCalculator`)

findings.finding: `ReportMinStartTS` has no InfoCache recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`, InfoSchema V2: I04). Lazy cursor fetch answers Go's `executor.Detach` over the physical plan (`tidb_executor::detach`), because the builder's operator tree is not Go's executor tree; A detached statement still publishes its completion through its record set's close, where Go never runs the abandoned `recordSet`'s `CloseRecordSet`

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

The MPP coordinator lowers a hand-built single-fragment scan DAG and refuses every pushed Selection, TopN and aggregation, where Go builds the fragment/task graph from the physical plan (including disaggregated compute placement)

`pkg/executor/mppcoordmanager` (`MPPCoordinatorManager`: coordinator registration, `detectAndDelete` expiry, the server address) and the RPC server's `ReportMPPTaskStatus` have no port, so TiFlash's task-status reports reach no coordinator; Go's coordinator only asks TiFlash for reports when its plan has a Limit above the table reader (`needReportExecutionSummary`), which the single-fragment scan never builds (M01)

PD's `serviceDiscovery` (`servicediscovery/service_discovery.go`) is not one owner here: member updates and the leader connection live in `pd/cluster.rs` / `pd/retry.rs`, with no per-member `serviceClient`, no `apiCandidateNodes` / `GetServiceClientByKind` (how Go picks a follower for a follower-handled region API) and no `checkServiceModeChanged`
No Cascades memo exploration/implementation in the production optimizer

SQL/PB signature construction and typed vector execution. The planner's `BuiltinFunctionUsageInc` (`expressionRewriter.newFunction`) is not called: it needs the function's `PbCode`, which a planner-built Rust function only gets at pushdown resolution. Go's `PbConverter` sends each builtin's own `PbCode`; this port resolves a signature again from the function's name, argument types and planned result type (`pushdown_catalog.rs` `resolve`), a second copy of each function class's signature choice that covers the functions Go's `scalarExprSupportedByTiKV` pushes. The planner decides pushability from `infer_pushdown.rs`'s name list and the executor again from that catalog's resolvability: two authorities where Go reads the builtin's `PbCode` once.
No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges

A CLUSTER_* table's TiDB-store reader sends Go's DAG (`builder_utils.rs`: `ConstructDAGReq`'s list-form `ToPB`, `SetHandleRanges`) and every TiDB rebuilds it with `coprocessor.rs`'s `PBPlanBuilder`; still apart from Go: `TIFLASH_REPLICA`'s TiDB-store reader runs its pushed plan as local executors where Go sends it to the DDL owner (`GetClusterTableCopDestination`, `SetTiDBServerID`); `SqlDigestTextRetriever`'s global pass hand-builds a TableScan plus DIGEST IN request (`ClusterPeerClient::scan_projected` via `peer_cluster_table_rows`) where Go's `RetrieveGlobal` runs `ExecRestrictedSQL` over CLUSTER_STATEMENTS_SUMMARY(_HISTORY); the reader records no cop runtime statistics from the responses (Go `selectResult.updateCopRuntimeStats`), so EXPLAIN ANALYZE's TableReader row lacks `cop_task`/`rpc_info` and its cop[tidb] rows show `N/A` where Go shows 0 rows; the requester answers its own task with its coprocessor handler in-process instead of over its status port
BRIE statements are classified but never executed
No DXF scheduler/executor managers composed

TopSQL is ported over pprof-rs (`tidb-cpuprofile`, `tidb-topsql-collector`, `tidb-topsql-reporter`, `tidb-topsql`): the status port serves `TopSQLPubSub`, the single-target sink reports to `top-sql.receiver-address`, each command labels its thread `{connID}_{sqlID}`, each statement registers its SQL and plan and labels the thread with both digests, and the profiler's TiDB CPU reaches PROCESSLIST and the statement summary. The DDL worker attaches each job step and each backfill task to the job's SQL (`tidb-ddl` `job_ctx.rs`, Go `ReorgContext.attachTopProfilingInfo`). The step's transaction carries the job's resource-group tagger (`getResourceGroupTaggerForTopSQL`, published into its statement kv context once the step loads the job). Unported: the DXF backfill executor's attach (O10) and the fast-reorg skip checks' (`checkIfTableReorgWorkCanSkip` / `checkIfTempIndexReorgWorkCanSkip`, D02), and the multi-statement prefetch's plan hand-off: `prefetchPointPlanKeys` reads (or locks) the point writes' keys before the statements run (`cluster_session_node/prefetch.rs`, with its `setResourceGroupTaggerForMultiStmtPrefetch`), but its point plans are not handed to the statements (Go `PointPlanKey`), which plan again. Executors register the statement's SQL and plan on their first `Next` with Top profiling on (`RegisterSQLAndPlanInExecForTopProfiling`, `SqlKillerCheckExec`); profiler labels follow Go's goroutine inheritance (`labels::inherit`) into the shuffle, hash-join build, checksum, coprocessor, slow-log parse, cluster-table fan-out, analyze and global-stats merge, DDL analyze workers and the MPP client's store probes

The DDL scheduler, systable manager, history and MDL readers scan records instead of running SQL on `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool`; the bootstrap stages raw rows; accounts load eagerly where Go loads per active user

Go's `ExecRestrictedSQL` / `ExecuteInternal` are methods of the issuing session (`withRestrictedSQLExecutor`); this port's executors are adapters beside it (`NodeRestrictedSql`, `SystemSqlExecutor`, `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor`, the plan replayer's `SessionSql`). The node's two apply `ExecOption`'s `SnapshotTS`, `AnalyzeVer`, `AnalyzeSnapshot`, `EnableDDLAnalyze` and `PartitionPruneMode` and restore them as Go's `useCurrentSession` / `getInternalSession` do, but with no issuing session they cannot inherit `OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes` / `SkipMissingPartitionStats` or append the internal session's warnings to the caller's (`IgnoreWarning`), and `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor` honours the options on the auto-analyze path alone. `rebuildSysVarCache` consumes the rows the domain's sysvar reload loop last read (`SysVarCacheDeps::table_contents`) where Go's runs `fetchTableValues` itself
